title: CHAPTER TEN. On the simplicity of God; definition
latin: CAPUT DECIMUM, De simplicitate Dei. Atque haec de secundo Dei attributo: sequitur tertium ejus attributum. I. Simplicitas videlicet, quae est summa Dei perfectio, per quam is ab omni compositione liber est. SIMPLICITATIS vocabulum a rebus corporeis mutuamur. Dicitur autem simplicitas, quia non positivum aliquid, sed negationem compositionis potissimum notat.
english: CHAPTER TEN. On the simplicity of God.

And these things concerning the second attribute of God: there follows His third attribute. I. Namely simplicity, which is God's highest perfection, by which He is free from every composition. The vocabulary of SIMPLICITY we borrow from corporeal things. But it is called simplicity because it notes not something positive, but chiefly the negation of composition.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TEN. Concerning ye simplicity belonging toward God. And these things concerning ye second attribute belonging toward God: His third attribute follows. I. Namely simplicity, which God's highest perfection is, by which from every composition free He is. Ye vocabulary belonging toward SIMPLICITY from corporeal things we borrow. But simplicity it is called because not something positive, but chiefly ye negation belonging toward composition it notes.

title: Simplicity proper to God; not univocal with creaturely simplicity
latin: Haec proprietas ita Deo convenit, ut creaturis non nisi umbram tenuem tribuamus. Neque compositionem rationis simplicitati divinae, non realem, adversari putamus. Quapropter simplicitas Dei non est eadem quae in creaturis, sed eminentior, ab omni compositione substantiali & accidentali remota.
english: This property so belongs to God that to creatures we attribute only a thin shadow. Nor do we think a composition of reason — not real — fights against the divine simplicity. Therefore God's simplicity is not the same as that in creatures, but more eminent, removed from every substantial and accidental composition.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): This property so unto God belongs that unto creatures only a thin shadow we attribute. Nor a composition belonging toward reason — not real — against ye divine simplicity to fight do we think. Therefore God's simplicity ye same as that in creatures is not, but more eminent, from every substantial plus accidental composition removed.

title: Demonstration from Scripture: spirit, first being
latin: Demonstramus Deum esse simplicem. PRIMO, sacrae Scripturae testimoniis, quae Deum spiritum, lucem, & non constitutum ex partibus declarant. TERTIO, quia Servator noster Joh. 4.24. Deo tribuit, ut sit spiritus: verum tamen non est, Deum, cum spiritus dicitur, aliquid corporeum indigitari. QUARTO, quia est ens primum. Nam ens primum a seipso exsistit, & a nullo componitur. Quicquid enim ex componentibus est posterius, adeoque non est simpliciter ens primum, nec omnino independens.
english: We demonstrate that God is simple. FIRST, by the testimonies of sacred Scripture, which declare God spirit, light, and not constituted from parts. THIRD, because our Savior (John 4:24) attributes to God that He is spirit: yet it is not true that when God is called spirit something corporeal is indicated. FOURTH, because He is the first being. For the first being exists from itself and is composed from none. For whatever is later from its components is therefore not simply the first being, nor altogether independent.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): We demonstrate that God simple is. FIRST, by ye testimonies belonging toward sacred Scripture, which God spirit, light, plus not constituted from parts declare. THIRD, because our Savior (John 4:24) unto God that He spirit is attributes: yet it is not true that when God spirit is called something corporeal is indicated. FOURTH, because ye first being He is. For ye first being from itself exists plus from none is composed. For whatever later from its components is therefore not simply ye first being, nor altogether independent.

title: From infinity and freedom from every composition
latin: SEXTO, id est omnium evidentissimum ab infinita Dei perfectione. SEPTIMO, Deum ab omni prorsus compositione esse liberum. Quicquid enim compositum est, imperfectius est eo quod simplex est; & ens infinitum compositionem non patitur.
english: SIXTH, and this is the most evident of all, from God's infinite perfection. SEVENTH, that God is free from every composition whatsoever. For whatever is composite is more imperfect than that which is simple; and an infinite being does not suffer composition.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): SIXTH, plus this ye most evident belonging toward all is, from God's infinite perfection. SEVENTH, that God from every composition whatsoever free is. For whatever composite is more imperfect than that which simple is; plus an infinite being composition does not suffer.

title: First genus of substantial composition: genus and difference — rejected
latin: PRIMUM substantialis compositionis genus, distinctum ex genere & differentia. Omne verum genus est univocum. Atqui nullum commune genus Deo cum rebus caeteris, neque differentia proprie dicta. Deus non potest restringi ad aliquod praedicamentum seu genus, sed supra omnia genera & extra ea est. Ad hoc primum genus compositionis reduximus quoque compositionem ex essentia & exsistentia.
english: The FIRST genus of substantial composition is that distinguished from genus and difference. Every true genus is univocal. But there is no common genus for God with the other things, nor a difference properly so called. God cannot be restricted to some predicament or genus, but is above all genera and outside them. To this first genus of composition we have also reduced composition from essence and existence.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye FIRST genus belonging toward substantial composition that from genus plus difference distinguished is. Every true genus univocal is. But no common genus for God with ye other things there is, nor a difference properly so called. God unto some predicament or genus restricted cannot be, but above all genera plus outside them is. Unto this first genus belonging toward composition also composition from essence plus existence we have reduced.

title: Further substantial composition genera (matter/form; integral parts) rejected
latin: TERTIUM compositionis substantialis genus est, quo ex materia & forma. At ista compositio in Deum non cadit. QUARTUM compositionis genus, quo substantia ex partibus integralibus. QUINTUM genus compositionis substantialis est ex actuario & potentiali. Haec autem in Deum non cadunt, quia aperta Scriptura & ratione refutantur.
english: The THIRD genus of substantial composition is that from matter and form. But that composition does not fall upon God. The FOURTH genus of composition is that by which a substance is from integral parts. The FIFTH genus of substantial composition is from the actual and the potential. But these do not fall upon God, because they are refuted by open Scripture and reason.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye THIRD genus belonging toward substantial composition that from matter plus form is. But that composition upon God does not fall. Ye FOURTH genus belonging toward composition that by which a substance from integral parts is. Ye FIFTH genus belonging toward substantial composition from ye actual plus ye potential is. But these upon God do not fall, because by open Scripture plus reason they are refuted.

title: No accidental composition in God
latin: HACTENUS vidimus in Deum non cadere ullam compositionem substantialem. Sequitur de accidentali. Deus non est mutabilis, ut inferius probabitur. Integralis non est, quia Deus proprie non est quantus & extensus. Quicquid accidentale in creaturis est, in Deo est substantia ipsa.
english: THUS FAR we have seen that no substantial composition falls upon God. There follows concerning the accidental. God is not mutable, as will be proved below. He is not integral, because God properly is not quantified and extended. Whatever is accidental in creatures is in God the substance itself.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): THUS FAR we have seen that no substantial composition upon God falls. Concerning ye accidental there follows. God mutable is not, as below will be proved. Integral He is not, because God properly quantified plus extended is not. Whatever accidental in creatures is, in God ye substance itself is.

title: Against world-soul and corporeal composition of God
latin: Deus non est anima mundi, nec materiae terminus ab agente productus, quia est ens primum. Idea in Deo non est aliud a Deo. Deus gubernator mundi est, sed non ut anima, neque ut nauta indigens navi, sed longe eminentius sola sua bonitate, nulla necessitate gubernans & vivificans omnia.
english: God is not the soul of the world, nor a term of matter produced by an agent, because He is the first being. The idea in God is not other than God. God is the governor of the world, but not as a soul, nor as a sailor needing a ship, but far more eminently governing and vivifying all things by His goodness alone, with no necessity.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): God ye soul belonging toward ye world is not, nor a term belonging toward matter by an agent produced, because ye first being He is. Ye idea in God other than God is not. God ye governor belonging toward ye world is, but not as a soul, nor as a sailor a ship needing, but far more eminently by His goodness alone, with no necessity, all things governing plus vivifying.

title: Pastoral close of Cap. 10; Cap. 11 next — Cap. 10 COMPLETE
latin: Piae ac Theologicae prudentiae est, de hoc Dei attributo Ecclesiam sic erudire, ut nihil eorum deferatur ad suggestum, quae a plebis captu sunt remota; potissimum autem haec duo inculcentur. 1. Deo id semper esse attribuendum, quod et perfectissimum est & intellectu divinitus colluminato percipi potest. 2. Iis, quae in contrarium incidunt, animum non cruciandum, sed potius in sanita ignorantiae nostrae confessione acquiescendum esse, ut Deo interim illibata omnis perfectionis gloria maneat.
english: It belongs to pious and theological prudence so to instruct the Church concerning this attribute of God that nothing of those things remote from the people's capacity be brought to the pulpit; but especially these two are to be inculcated. 1. That is always to be attributed to God which is both most perfect and can be perceived by an intellect divinely illuminated. 2. That the mind is not to be tormented by those things which fall out to the contrary, but rather to acquiesce in a sane confession of our ignorance, that meanwhile the unimpaired glory of every perfection may remain for God.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Unto pious plus theological prudence it belongs so ye Church concerning this attribute belonging toward God to instruct that nothing belonging toward those things from ye people's capacity remote unto ye pulpit be brought; but especially these two are to be inculcated. 1. That always unto God to be attributed is which both most perfect is plus by an intellect divinely illuminated can be perceived. 2. That ye mind by those things which unto ye contrary fall out is not to be tormented, but rather in a sane confession belonging toward our ignorance to acquiesce is, that meanwhile ye unimpaired glory belonging toward every perfection for God may remain.
